packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of
this leaf. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..018 of this packet. No web,
search, catalogue or edition was used. I have not tried to identify work or
author. One of the two rubrics on the leaf itself carries an abbreviated name;
I transcribe it as written and add only a bracketed expansion of the visible
abbreviation.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)

Observations
- Two faces of one leaf. image-001 = overview of face A; image-010 = overview of
  face B. Both upright, with a colour/centimetre target beside the leaf.
- Two columns per face, 39 written lines per column (an enlarged initial
  displaces part of one column on each face). Ruled lines visible.
- Rounded, upright bookhand with tall s, ę (e-caudata) and occasional æ,
  ampersand not used ("et" written out), -b; and -q; for -bus/-que, the "2-shaped"
  -orum sign, superscript sign for -us and -ur, punctus and punctus elevatus,
  and a question-like sign (rendered "?" below).
- No running titles visible. Upper margins are blank apart from two small dots
  above col. b on face A and above the intercolumn on face B.
- Rubrics in red capitals: face A col. a, one line ("ITẼ UÑ SUPRA."); face B
  col. b, two lines ("SERMO SC̃I GG P̃P . DE MORTA / LITATE.").
- Two large painted initials (gold letter with white-vine interlace on blue /
  maroon / dark-green panelled ground, red penwork corner finials): an E on
  face A col. a (about 8 text lines high) and an O on face B col. b (about
  6 text lines high). The words following each initial are in ink display
  capitals ("UANGELICA", "PORTET FR̃S").
- Marginal quotation marks (double comma-like strokes, ",,") stand in the left
  margin against four lines on face A col. b and three lines on face B col. a.
- No interlinear or marginal glosses. One superscript correction: an "s" added
  above the line end on face B col. b ("cupidita" + s).
- Damage: small hole on face A col. b line 10 / face B col. a line 10 (same
  hole, both sides); a rubbed/brown stain at lower right of face A col. b
  (lines 32-34) and matching weak ink on face B; edges of leaf irregular at the
  gutter side. Otherwise fully legible.

Tentative interpretation (not observation)
- Three text units are present: the end of one piece (face A col. a lines 1-14,
  closing with a doxology and "am̃"); a second piece beginning at the E initial
  and ending with a doxology on face B col. b line 21; and a third piece
  beginning at the O initial. The rubric "ITẼ UÑ SUPRA" appears to refer back to
  a heading on a preceding leaf that is not in this packet. Which face is recto
  is not determinable from the images alone; the text runs continuously
  face A col. a -> col. b -> face B col. a -> col. b, so face A precedes face B.

2. SPANS SELECTED / UNREAD
The script is clear enough that I read every line covered by the native tiles,
i.e. both columns of both faces complete (4 x 39 lines), with no unread areas.
Tiles overlap by about three lines top and bottom; overlap lines are marked
"(= ...)" and are not additional text. Line numbers are counted from the top of
each tile image; a line cut by the tile edge is still counted.

Conventions: abbreviation marks kept (ũ ẽ ã õ ñ etc. = macron/stroke over the
letter; ' = suspension stroke); proposed expansions in ( ); ę = e-caudata;
"?" at the end of a clause = the manuscript's interrogative sign; a hyphen at
line end reproduces the scribe's own hyphen stroke where one is written.
